# Stability tiers

Every command, export format and integration Quarto-Needs ships carries a
stability tier. The tier says what you may rely on, and what may change under
you.

The tiers are declared once, in `src/quarto_needs/surface.py`. The table
below, the `--help` output, the runtime warning and the support contract in
the README are all rendered or verified against that module, so a command
cannot be listed here at one tier and behave as another. Tests fail if this
chapter falls behind the registry.

## The three tiers

**Stable.** Covered by Semantic Versioning. A breaking change requires a major
release. Documented in this manual and exercised across the full CI matrix --
Python 3.10 through 3.14 on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows. If you build a pipeline
on stable surface, a minor upgrade will not break it.

**Preview.** Functional and tested, and used by this project's own CI. The
interface may still change in a minor release, and any such change gets a
CHANGELOG entry. Preview is not a warning about quality; it is a statement
that the shape of the interface is not yet settled.

**Experimental.** May change or be removed at any time, without a deprecation
period and without a CHANGELOG entry. Prints one line to stderr when invoked.
Does not block a release: an experimental feature that breaks is not a release
blocker, which is precisely why it cannot carry a compatibility promise.

## What "outside the stability contract" means in practice

For experimental surface, concretely:

- **No compatibility promise.** Flags, output shape, exit codes and the
  feature's existence may all change in a patch release.
- **No mandatory CHANGELOG entry.** Changes may land unannounced. The tier is
  the announcement.
- **Does not block a release.** A failing experimental feature does not hold
  up a version that is otherwise ready.
- **Warns at runtime.** One line on stderr, never stdout, so machine-readable
  output stays byte-identical. Set
  `QUARTO_NEEDS_SUPPRESS_EXPERIMENTAL_WARNING=1` to silence it. There is no
  command-line flag for this on purpose: a flag would have to be added to
  every subparser, including the ones that never reach argparse, recreating
  the duplication this registry removed.

Everything else -- stable and preview surface -- is inside the contract, with
preview carrying the weaker of the two promises.

## The complete surface

The `Layer` column records how a command reaches its implementation:
`argparse` commands are parsed by the main parser, `dispatch` commands are
intercepted before argparse runs. It is an implementation detail, listed here
because it is what the non-divergence tests bind to.

| Surface | Tier | Layer | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scan` | stable | argparse | Parse project and write .quarto-needs/needs.json |
| `check` | stable | argparse | Validate the requirements graph |
| `coverage` | stable | argparse | Print coverage metrics |
| `trace` | stable | argparse | Show upstream/downstream traceability |
| `export` | stable | argparse | Export canonical graph JSON |
| `quality` | stable | argparse | Evaluate scoped metrics, findings, and configured gates |
| `query` | stable | argparse | Evaluate a named query and print its ordered IDs |
| `evidence` | preview | argparse | Validate machine evidence against the engineering graph |
| `evidence check` | preview | argparse | Check a pytest evidence artifact against the current graph |
| `baseline` | stable | argparse | Create or inspect a canonical baseline |
| `baseline create` | stable | argparse | Write a baseline for the current graph |
| `baseline inspect` | stable | argparse | Summarize an existing baseline |
| `diff` | stable | argparse | Compare a baseline against the current graph |
| `impact` | stable | argparse | Explain what a baseline's changes reach |
| `suspect --git BASE..HEAD` | preview | dispatch | Traceability claims needing review after a change |
| `pr-report --git BASE..HEAD` | preview | dispatch | Combined change/impact/suspect review report |
| `github-report --git BASE..HEAD` | preview | dispatch | Summary, annotations, and check projection for GitHub |
| `diff --git BASE..HEAD` | preview | dispatch | Compare two committed Git states instead of a baseline |
| `impact --git BASE..HEAD` | preview | dispatch | Compare two committed Git states instead of a baseline |
| `evidence attest` | preview | dispatch | Sign and record an evidence attestation |
| `lsp` | preview | dispatch | Run the language server over stdio |
| `export --format reqif\|jsonld` | preview | dispatch | ReqIF 1.2 and JSON-LD interchange projections |
| `variant list\|show NAME` | experimental | dispatch | Inspect configured build variants |
| `migrate SOURCE` | experimental | dispatch | Migration plans for sphinx-needs, doorstop, strictdoc, openfasttrace, reqif |
| `oslc discover\|catalog\|query\|write` | experimental | dispatch | Bounded OSLC RM federation: read-only discovery/query and a reviewed write path |
| `export --format json` | stable | argparse | Export projection |
| `export --format csv` | stable | argparse | Export projection |
| `export --format markdown` | stable | argparse | Export projection |
| `export --format sarif` | preview | argparse | Export projection |
| `export --format junit` | preview | argparse | Export projection |
| `export --format reqif` | preview | dispatch | Export projection |
| `export --format jsonld` | preview | dispatch | Export projection |
| Quarto pre-render | stable | not a command | The project pre-render contributed by the Quarto extension |
| Documented non-C4 shortcodes | stable | not a command | need, need-table, need-graph, need-coverage and the other documented shortcodes |
| C4 projections | experimental | not a command | need-c4 and its PlantUML, D2 and Structurizr backends |
| GitHub Issues adapter | experimental | not a command | Reconciliation between needs and GitHub Issues |
| VS Code client | experimental | not a command | The language client packaged from editors/vscode |

## Promotion between tiers

A tier is a claim about maintenance, so moving up requires demonstrating that
the claim can be kept.

**Experimental to preview** requires all of:

- a stable interface that has not changed shape in at least one minor release;
- tests covering the normal path and the documented failure modes, running in
  the standard CI matrix rather than only locally;
- a manual chapter describing the feature, not just a `--help` line;
- deterministic output where the feature produces artifacts, verified by the
  reproducibility matrix like every other artifact-producing command.

**Preview to stable** additionally requires:

- no interface change across at least two minor releases;
- an explicit decision that the interface is worth supporting through a major
  version, recorded as an architecture decision;
- exercise on every supported platform and Python version, not only Linux;
- a migration path for any prior form, since after promotion removing it costs
  a major release.

Demotion is also possible and is a breaking change for stable surface, so it
follows the same rules as a removal: a major release, announced.

## Why the surface is narrow

A single maintainer cannot support a wide interface across many external
specifications. The decision recorded in
[Architecture decisions](architecture-decisions.qmd) is that a narrow stable
surface with a wide experimental one is more honest than a wide surface that
is nominally supported and actually is not. The tier table is where that
honesty is made checkable.
